title: Redcliff Capacity Accelerator & Data Residency Roadmap
summary: Monthly check-in focused on accelerating capacity top-up, sequencing EU edge activation, and clarifying data residency/contract implications. Agreed to run a short latency benchmark next week, share SOC2 docs and a proposed commitment ladder. Customer wants tighter SSO/KMS details and an outline for a phased EU go-live.
next_steps: Redwood to send revised commitment ladder + pricing by Wed 11/25
SE to schedule 1-hour latency + KV cache benchmark Wed 11/26
Send SOC2 certs and architecture note on KMS by 11/24
Customer to confirm internal sign-off stakeholders and go/no-go date by 11/30
action_items: Diego Morales - prepare benchmark harness and test plan (due 2026-11-26)
Alyssa Chen - send commitment ladder and draft SOW (due 2026-11-25)
Priya Kapoor - collate SOC2 + KMS integration notes and share (due 2026-11-24)
Marta Lopez - confirm go-live committee and dates (due 2026-11-30)
transcript:
[00:00] Alyssa Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, looks like we have about 55 minutes, uh, agenda is capacity accelerator and the EU data residency roadmap. Quick intros?
[00:12] Marta Lopez: Marta here, head of platform at Redcliff. Ethan, Samir, Nina with me.
[00:18] Ethan Park: Hey all.
[00:20] Diego Morales: Diego from Redwood SE, hey.
[00:23] Priya Kapoor: Priya from CSM.
[00:25] Alyssa Chen: Great. Quick update from our side: we've provisioned the burst pool for your US-West traffic and can shift some reserved GPU nodes into the EU pool once we have the commit ladder signed. We wanted to walk through sequencing and any compliance blockers.
[00:40] Samir Rao: On the compliance side, primary ask is data residency for EU customers. We need the logs and payloads to remain in the EU and KMS keys controlled by our vault. SSO also needs to be SAML 2.0 with SCIM.
[00:55] Diego Morales: Right, we support customer-managed KMS and can configure a VPC private control plane for the Private deployment. Small caveat: if you want on-prem key material via HSM, there's an addendum and slight delay on provisioning.
[01:10] Nina Foster: When you say "small caveat" what's the timeline impact?
[01:14] Diego Morales: Usually 2-3 weeks for HSM key integration depending on your HSM vendor and networking readiness. If you use hosted KMS with key ownership, it's faster, like 3-5 days.
[01:25] Ethan Park: We prefer HSM but want to avoid long runway delays. Could we stage: hosted KMS first, then HSM swap?
[01:32] Priya Kapoor: Customers do that often — we can do a staged migration: hosted key for initial EU activation, then rotate to HSM during the canary window.
[01:40] Marta Lopez: Okay that helps. Next is capacity. Our models ramped unexpectedly; 95th pct latency in prod spiked last week. We need guaranteed throughput for peak windows and lower cost for steady-state.
[01:55] Alyssa Chen: Yes, that's exactly the capacity accelerator use case — we propose a commitment ladder: base reserved capacity for steady load + accelerator top-ups for peak windows. The top-ups shift to dedicated burst pools but billed at a different rate.
[02:10] Ethan Park: Can you show the numbers?
[02:13] Alyssa Chen: Sure, Diego — could you pull up the cost breakdown? (brief pause) Sorry on the call, I can't share screen in transcript but Diego, quick high level?
[02:25] Diego Morales: High level: base 8 GPUs reserved, handles ~120 rps depending on seq len. For accelerator, add burst blocks of 4 GPUs for up to 4 hours; cost per token for burst is about 30% higher than reserved, but effective unit cost during idle periods is lower because you don't pay for unused reserved capacity. We also recommend enabling prefix caching — that reduces tokens by ~18% for your chat flows.
[02:55] Samir Rao: Prefix caching raises questions for us — where is the cache located, how is it encrypted, and does it leave the EU?
[03:05] Diego Morales: Good question. Cache can be colocated in the same EU geocluster; data-at-rest encryption uses the same KMS path you choose, and we can configure TTLs and eviction to reduce surface area. I will add a note to the architecture doc.
[03:20] Marta Lopez: About latency: we're seeing a 60ms tail for short queries and about 400ms for long seq. Any levers?
[03:27] Diego Morales: A couple: 1) choose a model variant optimized for decoder perf; 2) scale kv cache nodes to reduce warmup; 3) enable smaller batch sizes with lower token latency at cost of throughput. We can run a short benchmark that mirrors your seq length distribution.
[03:45] Ethan Park: Let's do a benchmark. What's the cadence?
[03:48] Diego Morales: We propose a 1-hour harness: sample traffic from your staging, run against reserved vs burst pools, and measure p50/p95/p99. I can script that and share results.
[03:58] Alyssa Chen: Ok that maps to an action item.
[04:00] [05:00] (conversation continues — planning specifics, slight crosstalk)
[08:12] Priya Kapoor: On contracts: if you move to a longer term for base reserved capacity we can offer a stepped discount — the commitment ladder I mentioned — and include an EU activation credit to offset migration work.
[08:25] Marta Lopez: How binding is the ladder? Internal procurement needs optionality in Q1.
[08:30] Alyssa Chen: The ladder is a structured agreement — base term with optional accelerator buckets you can purchase on-demand. We can craft an amendment that keeps Q1 opt-out but secures priority provisioning windows for you.
[08:45] Samir Rao: Also need to see audit logs — retention and format. We have to forward to our SIEM in Frankfurt.
[08:52] Diego Morales: Audit log export to your S3 in eu-central-1 is supported. We also have a syslog/forwarder option. Logs are encrypted with your KMS key. I'll add the export instructions to the doc set.
[09:05] Marta Lopez: Great. Any competitors in your pricing model conversation?
[09:09] Alyssa Chen: They mentioned GiantCloudAI and EdgeServe as references earlier — we discussed how Redwood's unified runtime gives more predictable unit economics.
[09:20] Ethan Park: One more technical point — can you do a canary for the EU activation that falls back to US if the latency/throughput thresholds fail?
[09:28] Diego Morales: Absolutely. We have smart routing rules — canary rollout with automatic fallback to US-hosted model variant. You can set SLO thresholds and a circuit breaker.
[09:38] Nina Foster: Are there any limitations on model types for EU cluster? We use a custom fine-tuned Llama variant.
[09:44] Diego Morales: Custom models are supported but for private deployments we do an onboarding validation; for hosted we need to check licensing and quantization path. There might be a small delta in perf for quantized vs full float. We'll validate during the benchmark.
[09:58] Marta Lopez: Let's talk timeline. We want EU live for a beta cohort by mid-December; full ramp by end of Q1. Is that realistic?
[10:08] Alyssa Chen: Mid-December beta is tight but possible if we 1) sign the ladder this week, 2) do the benchmark next week, and 3) prioritize KMS onboarding. That gives ~3-4 weeks for initial setup.
[10:20] Marta Lopez: Ok we'll try to accelerate internal approvals.
[10:24] Samir Rao: One more — vulnerability scanning and pen test schedule?
[10:27] Priya Kapoor: We publish our pen test cadence in the security pack; we can also include a SOC2 Type II report and engagement checklist.
[10:35] Alyssa Chen: Quick recap before we wrap: redwood items are send commitment ladder & SOW, run benchmark, share SOC2/KMS notes; customer to confirm stakeholders and internal timeline. Any final questions?
[10:48] Ethan Park: No, that's it.
[10:50] Marta Lopez: Sounds good, thanks.
[10:52] Alyssa Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with dates.
[10:55] [54:30] (wrap up, small social chat)
[54:45] Diego Morales: I'll post the test plan to the shared drive after this.
[54:50] Priya Kapoor: I'll attach security docs.
[54:55] Alyssa Chen: Ending call, talk soon.
[55:00] END
